passage:
Ten minutes into a rainy Sunday, Chaitanya stood at the sofa with drooping shoulders. "I'm bored. What do I do? Can I have the tablet?" Papa Sumit did not reach for it. He slid over an empty cardboard box, some tape and a pair of blunt scissors. After a grumble, Chaitanya cut a door into the box, then a window, and by lunch the box was a bus with a very serious driver.
By nine, Chaitanya was reading books meant for much older children and asking questions about how stars burn. In class the lessons felt slow, and Chaitanya rubbed out drawings that were not exactly right. At break the other children were playing kabaddi, and Chaitanya stood at the edge of the game, unsure how to join. Mummy Neelam found the fine marks and the long silences at home. That evening she skipped the quiz about facts and sat on the floor with a board game. "Your turn," she said. Chaitanya laughed for the first time all week, and lost happily.

qa.q: What did Papa Sumit give Chaitanya instead of the tablet?
qa.a: He gave Chaitanya an empty cardboard box, some tape and a pair of blunt scissors.

qa.q: How does the rainy Sunday at age five connect to the picture of Chaitanya at nine?
qa.a: At five, Chaitanya said bored and asked for the tablet, but with a cardboard box, tape and time the box became a bus. At nine, Chaitanya was reading books for older children yet felt bored in class, rubbed out drawings and stood at the edge of the game, so Mummy skipped the quiz and played a board game with the whole child.

qa.q: What was Chaitanya feeling while standing at the edge of the kabaddi game?
qa.a: Chaitanya felt shy and left out, wanting to join in but not knowing how to begin.

qa.q: What would you advise Mummy Neelam to do to help Chaitanya find friends?
qa.a: She could arrange a small, easy play meet-up with one or two children around a game Chaitanya enjoys, and keep making time for play and comfort at home.

grounding: A child's boredom in early childhood (4068) and the advanced-mind-but-ordinary-child needs seen years later (4519) in the same family.
